reason: The cited evidence supports the general benefits of coherent nanoprecipitates in W-based HEAs (E1) and the high-temperature microstructural stability of such alloys (E2), but none of the passages mention copper addition, Cu nanoprecipitate formation, or any thermal conductivity measurements. The key premises about Cu-induced conductivity enhancement and the specific 10–20% improvement are therefore unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates in W-based HEAs can enhance strength and ductility without causing embrittlement.
W-based HEAs can be processed to have a stable BCC dendritic microstructure that resists high-temperature degradation.
Tungsten is a leading plasma-facing material with high thermal conductivity and thermomechanical stability.
Adding ~3 wt% Cu to a W-based HEA will form coherent Cu nanoprecipitates that create additional electron conduction pathways.
These Cu nanoprecipitates will boost thermal conductivity by 10–20% without reducing yield strength or ductility by more than 5%.
